questions.question: The speed of a boat down the stream is 125% of the speed in still water. If the boat takes 30 minutes to cover 20 km in still water, then how much time (in hours) will it take to cover 15 km upstream?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a boat down the stream is 125% of the speed in still water. If the boat takes 30 minutes to cover 20 km in still water, then how much time (in hours) will it take to cover 15 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio Downstream : Still water = 125% : 100% = 5 : 4

Stream speed ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 part, so Upstream speed ratio = 4 − 1 = 3 parts.

Speed in still water (4 parts) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hr = 40 km/h.

Upstream speed (3 parts) = (40 ÷ 4) × 3 = 30 km/h.

Time for 15 km upstream = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour.

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Speed downstream = 125% of speed in still water.

⇒ Time taken to cover 20 km in still water = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours.

Formula Used:

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = Boat Speed (B) + Stream Speed (S)

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = Boat Speed (B) − Stream Speed (S)

Calculations:

⇒ Speed in still water (B) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hours = 40 km/h

⇒ Speed downstream (D) = 125% of 40 = 1.25 × 40 = 50 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream (S) = D − B = 50 − 40 = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed upstream (U) = B − S = 40 − 10 = 30 km/h

⇒ Time to cover 15 km upstream = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

⇒ Time = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.

Additional Information

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: B = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: S = (D − U) ÷ 2

Average Speed of Journey

If a boat goes a certain distance downstream and comes back upstream, the average speed is (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.question: Two persons started running on a circular track at a speed of 20 m/s and 30 m/s in opposite directions. If the circumference of the circular track is 100 m, find at how many distinct points they will cross each other?
questions.questionHtml: Two persons started running on a circular track at a speed of 20 m/s and 30 m/s in opposite directions. If the circumference of the circular track is 100 m, find at how many distinct points they will cross each other?
questions.solution:
Given : 

Speed of 1st person = 20 m/s

Speed of the 2nd person = 30 m/s

Circumference of the Track = 100 m

Concept used :

Speed = Distance covered / Time taken

Calculation :

The time taken by the first person to complete a full lap is 100 m / 20 m/s = 5 seconds. 

The time taken by the second person to complete a full lap is 100 m / 30 m/s = 10/3 seconds.

​The LCM of 5 seconds and 10/3 seconds is 10 seconds, which means they will end up in the same initial positions after 10 seconds.

Let the two persons cross each other for the first time after x seconds.

Then, total distance covered by 1st person = 20x and the 2nd person = 30x

Now, the total distance covered by both the person = Circumference of the track ⇒ 30x + 20x = 100m ⇒ 50x = 100m ⇒ x = 2 s

∴ The two persons will cross each other for the first time after 2 seconds.

After 2 seconds, the first person will be at the starting point and the second person will be at the opposite point on the track.

The two persons will cross each other again after 2 seconds, and then again after 2 seconds, and so on.

So in 10 seconds they will meet = 10/2 = 5 times

Therefore, the two persons will cross each other at 5 distinct points on the track.

Shortcut Trick

S1 = 20 m/s and S2 = 30 m/s

S1/S2 = 2/3

They are running in opposite directions so they will meet each other at distinct points = 2 + 3 = 5

questions.question: If x 2 - 7x + 1 = 0, and 0 < x < 1, what is the value of x 2 - \(\frac{1}{x^2}\) ?
questions.questionHtml: If x2 - 7x + 1 = 0, and 0 < x < 1, what is the value of x2 - \(\frac{1}{x^2}\) ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From x2 − 7x + 1 = 0, divide by x to get x + 1/x = 7.

If x + 1/x = a, then x − 1/x = ±√(a2 − 4).

Since 0 < x < 1, x − 1/x must be negative, so x − 1/x = −√(72 − 4) = −√45 = −3√5.

We need x2 − 1/x2 = (x + 1/x)(x − 1/x) = 7 × (−3√5) = −21√5.

∴ The correct answer is −21√5.

Alternate Method

Given:

x2 − 7x + 1 = 0 and 0 < x < 1

Formula Used:

(a − b)2 = (a + b)2 − 4ab

a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b)

Calculations:

⇒ x2 − 7x + 1 = 0

Divide the equation by x:

⇒ x − 7 + 1/x = 0

⇒ x + 1/x = 7

Using the algebraic identity:

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = (x + 1/x)2 − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = 72 − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = 49 − 4 = 45

⇒ x − 1/x = ±√45 = ±3√5

Since 0 < x < 1, 1/x > x, so (x − 1/x) is negative.

⇒ x − 1/x = −3√5

Now find the value of x2 − 1/x2:

⇒ x2 − 1/x2 = (x + 1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ x2 − 1/x2 = 7 × (−3√5)

⇒ x2 − 1/x2 = −21√5

∴ The correct answer is −21√5.

Additional Information

Higher Powers Identity

If x + 1/x = a, then x2 + 1/x2 = a2 − 2, and x3 + 1/x3 = a3 − 3a.

Difference Identity

If x − 1/x = a, then x2 + 1/x2 = a2 + 2, and x3 − 1/x3 = a3 + 3a.

Sum to Difference Conversion

(x + 1/x)2 − (x − 1/x)2 = 4. This is extremely useful for shifting between sum and difference of reciprocals.

questions.question: In ₹150, B buys 10 pens for ₹8 each, 10 erasers for ₹5 each and some sharpeners for ₹4 each. What is the average price per item in ₹?

⇒ Cost of pens = 10 × 8 = ₹80

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

When different quantities (n1, n2...) have different prices (p1, p2...), the weighted average = (n1p1 + n2p2 + ...) ÷ (n1 + n2 + ...).

Average Price Concept

The average price represents the uniform cost if all items were bought at the same price while maintaining the same total expenditure.

Unit Price = Total Cost of specific items ÷ Number of units of those items.

questions.question: If \(\triangle \mathrm{ABC} \sim \triangle \mathrm{PQR}\) , AB = 4 cm, PQ = 6 cm, QR = 9 cm and RP = 12 cm, then find the perimeter of \(\triangle \mathrm{ABC} \text {. }\)
questions.questionHtml: If \(\triangle \mathrm{ABC} \sim \triangle \mathrm{PQR}\), AB = 4 cm, PQ = 6 cm, QR = 9 cm and RP = 12 cm, then find the perimeter of \(\triangle \mathrm{ABC} \text {. }\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles = Ratio of their perimeters.

Side ratio (ABC : PQR) = AB ÷ PQ = 4 ÷ 6 = 2 ÷ 3.

Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP = 6 + 9 + 12 = 27 cm.

Perimeter of ΔABC = 27 × (2 ÷ 3) = 18 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, AB = 4 cm, PQ = 6 cm, QR = 9 cm, and RP = 12 cm.

Formula Used: For two similar triangles, Perimeter1 ÷ Perimeter2 = Side1 ÷ Side2.

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = 6 + 9 + 12 = 27 cm

⇒ AB ÷ PQ = Perimeter of ΔABC ÷ Perimeter of ΔPQR

⇒ 4 ÷ 6 = Perimeter of ΔABC ÷ 27

⇒ 2 ÷ 3 = Perimeter of ΔABC ÷ 27

⇒ Perimeter of ΔABC = (2 × 27) ÷ 3

⇒ Perimeter of ΔABC = 54 ÷ 3 = 18 cm

∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.

Additional Information

Similarity Ratios

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Area Ratio Property

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area1 ÷ Area2 = (Side1 ÷ Side2)2.

Criteria for Similarity

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy the AA (Angle-Angle), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), or SSS (Side-Side-Side) conditions.

questions.question: The third proportional between 25 and 35 is:

Shortcut Trick

Mean Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the mean proportional x is calculated as x = √(ab).

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional x satisfies a : b :: c : x, resulting in x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continuous Proportion

Three non-zero numbers a, b, c are in continuous proportion if a : b = b : c.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Symptoms like nervousness, increased heart rate and feeling weak are some of the starting signs of anxiety.

B. Whereas anxiety attacks, sweating, trembling and having a feeling of impending danger might suggest advanced anxiety levels.

C. Most people don't even realise they have anxiety or take corrective measures until it amplifies and gets out of control.

D. Anxiety is a sad reality of today's time that has plagued a number of us in a variety of different ways.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is DCAB.

Key Points

  • 'D' - This sentence introduces the topic of anxiety setting the tone for the coming sentences. A general statement about the prevalence of anxiety in contemporary society provides an excellent introduction.
  • 'C' - This sentence logically follows 'D' in the narrative. After introducing anxiety as a pervasive issue, it discusses how many people fail to recognize they're suffering from it until it becomes severe.
  • 'A' - After discussing the fact that many people fail to recognize their anxiety, it's logical to now discuss the onset symptoms of anxiety. Hence, 'A' follows 'C'.
  • 'B' - This sentence elaborates on escalated symptoms, following logically from 'A', which provides the initial symptoms of anxiety.

Therefore, the correct answer is: DCAB.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

Additional Information

  • Option 2: Incorrect. The present tense "is invented" does not fit the past tense of the given sentence.

  • Option 4: Incorrect. While it is grammatically correct, it implies that the invention occurred recently.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Mendel's simple 'Laws of heredity' came to be widely known and were uncritically assumed to apply to all human characteristics.

B. With Charles Darwin's popularisation of the concept of evolution, man became interested in his biological origins and affiliations.

C. Starting with the work on heredity of Gregor Mendel in the 1860s and the recognition of its significance in 1900, interest shifted to the problem of man's ontogenetic origins.

D. This interest was centred on man's phylogenetic origins.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BDCA".

Key Points

  • Sentence B introduces the topic of man's biological origins and affiliations. 
  • Sentence D specifies that the interest was focused on man's phylogenetic origins. 
  • Sentence C provides a timeline of the shift in interest, starting with Mendel's work on heredity and ending with the recognition of its significance.
  • The paragraph discusses the shift in interest from Mendel's laws of heredity to man's ontogenetic and phylogenetic origins. 

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4".

Additional Information

  • Option 1 (ADCB) starts with the discussion of Mendel's laws and ends with the focus on man's phylogenetic origins, which is not the correct order.
  • Option 2 (DCAB) starts with the discussion of man's biological origins and ends with the introduction of Mendel's laws, which is not the correct order.
  • Option 3 (CDBA) starts with the timeline of the shift in interest and ends with the discussion of Mendel's laws, which is not the correct order.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "depend".

Key Points

  • The reason "depend" is the most suitable option for the sentence is due to its meaning and context.
  • "Depend" is used when something or someone relies on or needs someone or something else for support, help, or existence.
  • In the context of the sentence: "We need the energy to move and we (1) ______ on oil for it."
    • we are talking about our reliance on oil for energy.
    • Therefore, it makes sense to say that we "depend" on oil for it.
  • So, when we fill in the blank with the correct option, it reads: "We need the energy to move and we depend on oil for it."
  • This sentence implies that oil is a necessary or crucial source for our energy needs, since we "depend" on it.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4". 

Additional Information

  • Hang - This word often means to suspend or be suspended from above with the lower part dangling free and could not fit in the given context.
  • Turn - This can mean to cause to move in a particular direction by or as if by twisting, which does not make sense in the context provided.
  • Settle - This can mean to reach a decision or an agreement about something, or to pay a bill or debt, which does not suit the context here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "shall". 

Key Points

  • In the sentence "Without it, our jobs, our free time and our mobility (2) ______ all be very different," the word "shall" could work, but its usage is a bit more formal and somewhat less common in this context. 
  • We use "shall' when we are denoting a  specific context if we interpret the situation as kind of "prophetic" or "inevitable".
  • For this reason shall has been used, as we are talking about time when if energy is not present then there will most definitely be the results mentioned above. 
  • In this perspective, using "shall" intensifies the degree of certainty related to the change that will affect our jobs, free time, and mobility if oil is not available.
  • So, revisiting the sentence: "Without it, our jobs, our free time and our mobility shall all be very different," it implies there's a certainty about the possible drastic changes due to the absence of oil.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "consume". 

Key Points

  • "Consume" is a term often used to depict the utilization of a resource, especially oil, fuel, energy, or food. In this context, it refers to the amount of oil that is being used up by human activity.
  • So the sentence becomes "Every day we consume 70 million barrels of oil".

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1". 

Additional Information

  • "Devour" is a term typically used when referring to eating hastily or ravenously.
    • It carries a far more aggressive sentiment than is typically associated with the utilization of resources and is rarely used outside the context of food.
  • "Take" is a very general verb and would technically make sense in this context ("Every day we take 70 million barrels of oil").
    • However, it is less precise compared with "consume". "Take" could imply a simple act of possession rather than usage.
  • "Absorb" is usually used to describe a process where one thing becomes incorporated into another thing, usually in a passive manner.
    • This term is not typically used when referring to the usage of resources like oil.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "was founded". 

Key Points

  • "Was founded" is in the simple past passive voice, which makes sense in this context.
  • This option fits perfectly as it shows the action done by an unknown (or unimportant in this context) entity in past.
  • It states that in 1924, the company "Total" was established by someone.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2". 

  • So, the correct sentence would be: "Total was founded in 1924, and for many years it was a French state oil company. In 1999, Total joined Petrofina, the Belgian oil and gas company, and in 2000, Total merged with its main French competitor, Elf Aquitaine, and the name became Total Fina Elf. Now it's called Total again, and it's France's biggest company."

Additional Information

  • "Had founded" is in the past perfect tense and usually refers to an action that occurred before another past action.
    • Here, it does not work because there is no other past action to reference.
  • "Founded" on its own doesn't provide the necessary auxiliary verb (was or were) to signify passive voice in the past.
  • "Were founded" is incorrect because "Total" is a singular noun and "were" is used with plural nouns.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:

Key Points

  • "Merged" refers to when two or more entities become a single entity.
  • In our case, it could mean Total and Elf Aquitaine becoming one company.
  • This term is frequently used when two companies combine to form one.
  • Thus, the sentence should read: "In 2000, Total merged with its main French competitor, Elf Aquitaine, and the name became Total Fina Elf."

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1". 

Additional Information

  • "Combine" is typically used in a more general sense when two or more things are mixed together, but in a business context, it lacks the precision and connotation of two separate entities coming together to form a single one.
  • "Join" usually refers to becoming part of a group, team, or organization, and lacks the connotation that two separate entities become a new, single entity, which the context suggests.
  • "Incorporate" is typically used to refer to including something as part of something else, and it doesn't quite capture the meaning in this context.
